key_insight: ATLAS is a diffusion-based foundation sampler that generates Boltzmann-distributed amorphous structures directly from an energy function, enabling efficient sampling, thermodynamic estimation, and design of disordered materials.
engineering_relevance: It can cut the cost of exploring glassy energy landscapes by orders of magnitude, making inverse design and property optimization of metallic glasses and other amorphous materials more practical.
method: Uses an equivariant graph neural network to learn the reverse-time diffusion process over atomic configurations.
Generalizes across system size, temperature, and composition, with composition-amortized pretraining for reuse across materials.
Supports steering toward target observables and coupling to expensive interatomic potentials or LLM-guided search.
evidence_signal: In 2D Kob-Andersen systems, ATLAS matched parallel-tempering MCMC distributions and achieved below 0.2% free-energy error in the low-temperature glass regime with over 500-fold fewer energy evaluations.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the target energy model and pretrained coverage, so transfer to unfamiliar chemistries or highly inaccurate potentials may be limited.
paper_title: ATLAS: A Foundation Neural Sampler for Amorphous Materials
